statement: Whenever find_shortest_sub_array(nums) returns a result r, the integer r equals the minimum of h-l over all pairs (l,h) with 0 <= l < h <= n and degree(l,h) = D. The minimum is over a nonempty set because the whole array (0,n) has degree(0,n) = D.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 49999. Let n = len(nums). For 0 <= l < h <= n, let freq(l,h,v) be the number of indices j with l <= j < h and nums[j] = v, and let degree(l,h) be the maximum of freq(l,h,v) over values v occurring in nums[l..h) (equivalently, the maximum over i with l <= i < h of freq(l,h,nums[i])). Let D = degree(0,n). For a value v that occurs in nums, let first(v) be the smallest index i with nums[i]=v and last(v) the largest such index. The notation nums[l..h) denotes the contiguous subarray with indices l, l+1, ..., h-1.

statement: Let rev(nums) be the slice of length n defined by rev(nums)[i] = nums[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Whenever find_shortest_sub_array(nums) returns r and find_shortest_sub_array(rev(nums)) returns r', we have r = r'.

statement: Let V be the set of values occurring in nums. Let g be any function that is injective on V and satisfies 0 <= g(v) <= 49999 for every v in V, and let nums' be any slice of length n with nums'[i] = g(nums[i]) for all i with 0 <= i < n. Whenever find_shortest_sub_array(nums) returns r and find_shortest_sub_array(nums') returns r', we have r = r'.
